title: PersonaClaims/PresenceInfo do not match the persona claims the daemon actually emits
description:
persona-core/src/hvid.rs:8-35 exports `PersonaClaims` and `PresenceInfo` as "the exact JSON shape required by the spec" (hvid.rs:21). persona-grpc/src/service.rs:162-173 builds the persona object that actually goes into every JWT-SVID by hand with `serde_json::json!` and produces a different shape:

- hvid.rs:14 `attested_at: String` (documented RFC 3339) vs service.rs:169 `"attested_at": now_secs` — an integer.
- hvid.rs:16 `present_until: String` (documented RFC 3339) vs service.rs:170 `"present_until": present_until` — an integer.

So `serde_json::from_value::<PersonaClaims>(..)` on the persona object of a token this daemon issues fails with "invalid type: integer, expected a string". The public type that a consumer library would reach for is the one thing that cannot parse real output. grep confirms `PersonaClaims` has no non-test use anywhere in the workspace (only persona-core/src/lib.rs:15 re-export and its own tests) — nothing forces the two shapes to agree, so they drifted.

Related and part of the same fix: `PersonaClaims` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (hvid.rs:22) with no constructor, so external code cannot build one either; it can only be obtained by deserialization, which as shown does not work against real tokens.

The Unix-seconds choice itself is a tracked shortcut (ponytail comment at service.rs:155) — the finding here is the divergence and the unusable public type, not the timestamp format. Fix by having service.rs construct `PersonaClaims`/`PresenceInfo` and serialize it, so the type is the single definition of the wire shape, and add a constructor.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.51 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
